purpose: Turn a fully ranked, uncapped result into the budgeted SearchResponse the CLI prints, in the agent layer and never in core (docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md sections 7.5 and 9.1; 01-core-architecture.md section 10).
scope: crates/monokl/src/budget.rs behind the cli feature: Budget, apply_budget, count_tokens, and the SearchResponse truncation rendering in output/agent.rs. Takes plain arguments; does not call the search pipeline.
non_goals: The search pipeline and any ranking or re-ranking.
Budgeting other commands (symbols, dependents) or allocating one budget across a batch of operations.
Skipping an oversized block to keep filling with later smaller ones; the kept results are always a prefix in rank order.
Splitting or shortening a single block.

api_surface.name: Budget
api_surface.signature: pub struct Budget { pub max_results: usize, pub max_tokens: usize, pub max_bytes: usize }
api_surface.description: The three caps. Default is 50 results, 20,000 tokens, 2 MiB.

api_surface.name: apply_budget
api_surface.signature: pub fn apply_budget(ranked: Vec<RankedBlock>, total_before: usize, budget: &Budget, diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>) -> SearchResponse
api_surface.description: Keeps the longest rank-order prefix of blocks that fits all three caps and reports what was cut.

api_surface.name: count_tokens
api_surface.description: Exact o200k_base token count, falling back to the byte length above a byte cap.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Empty input returns no results, truncated false, no marker, zero bytes and tokens, and passes diagnostics through unchanged.
Blocks totalling exactly max_results, max_bytes or max_tokens are all kept with truncated false; one more block over any one limit keeps the prefix before it and sets truncated true.
When several limits would trip, the cut falls at the earliest block that breaks any limit, and results stay in the input order.
A first block larger than max_bytes yields zero results, truncated true and a marker; total_bytes and total_tokens are 0.
total_bytes is the summed code length and total_tokens the exact o200k_base count of the kept blocks; the byte-bound shortcut and the tokenizer give the same count for the same blocks.

A truncated response has total_blocks_before_truncation equal to total_before and a marker of the form 'showing K of N; refine the query with +term or -term' built from michi's truncation hint; an untruncated one has none.
Rendering a truncated SearchResponse through render_projection reports totalCount N and the marker as a help line.

linked_research: docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md section 10; docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md sections 7.5 and 9.1. No requirement@1 REQ-017 exists.
reasoning: Budgeting is an agent-layer step; core returns ranked results and counts only.
